hypotheses: Semantic interpretation improves exact authored-business-goal completion relative to a capable documented command parser.
Extra LLM experiment planning adds benefit relative to the same semantic interpretation followed by deterministic model comparison and pilot selection.
fairness: Identical observed numeric rows and goals for all methods. Reader and adaptive arms share one actual LLM interpretation. Both fit the same four recipes and have exactly two development pilot slots. All decisions use the same validation and final financial evaluator. Rules has no semantic LLM; that contrast tests language interpretation, not orchestration.
evaluation: 24 authored cases: six direct requests, six paraphrases, six revisions/negations and six ambiguous/unsupported requests. Expected specifications are evaluation-only; runtime validation checks schema and general authority, never expected answers. No final economic outcomes enter the planner. Finance uses independent final seeds and a 14-day return tail.

successCriteria.semantic: More exact supported/clarify outcomes than command parsing with no incorrect-ready outputs on the six unsupported cases. Report exact paired discordances and uncertainty; do not extrapolate to production.
successCriteria.adaptive: Equal or better exact completion and positive paired financial improvement after inference cost over the shared-reader workflow. If not established, prefer the shared-reader workflow.
successCriteria.recovery: Offline crash/resume tests preserve completed artifact and effect identities without repeated completed training, pilots or simulated publications.

limitations: Authored language benchmark; not representative merchant data or blinded human annotations.
Four recipes, two pilot slots and seven original features limit strategic headroom.
No production PayPal ROI or novel framework claim.
No new sandbox payments; existing receipts remain integration evidence.
